messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable modern Australian trade strategy game inspired by Squatter, featuring imports/exports, events, policy, climate, AI, 3D-style counters, sound, and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- User requested solo AI at multiple difficulty levels, online modes/lobbies, animated dice, music/sound/voices/weather effects, and touchscreen controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone browser game with solo AI and local pass-and-play; online matchmaking is not implemented because no server is available, and the in-game guide discloses this limitation.
- Used fictionalized game values and market shifts rather than live economic data; the guide discloses these are not forecasts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game UI, 20-space trade board, AI difficulty options, pass-and-play mode, market and policy actions, events, weather, investment, scoring, generated sound effects, and mobile action buttons.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Started a local static server on port 3002 and opened the page in Playwright. The only reported console error is a missing `/favicon.ico` (404).

### Active
- Browser verification is underway; game has not yet been tested through its interactive turn flow or captured in a screenshot.
- Changes are uncommitted.

### Blocked
- Real online matchmaking/lobbies, live trade data, full music, and voice acting require backend/data/audio resources not present in this project.

## Next Move
1. Click “OPEN THE TRADE DESK” in Playwright and verify board rendering, market/policy actions, dice roll, tile resolution, AI progression, and mobile layout.
2. Check for additional console errors and fix any gameplay issues found.
3. Optionally add a favicon or suppress the 404, then report assumptions and online-mode limitation to the user.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and board/counter styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, AI, events, economy, sound, and interactions.

## Important Context
- Local testing URL: `http://localhost:3002`; server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` succeeded; its initial console error was `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico:0`.

## Objective
- Build a playable modern Australian trade strategy game inspired by Squatter, with trade, climate, policy, events, AI opponents, and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- The original request called for real-time import/export data, solo AI difficulty levels, online modes and lobbies, animated dice, music/sound/voices/weather, and touchscreen controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone browser game with solo AI and local pass-and-play; online matchmaking is not implemented without a server.
- Use fictionalized market values and shifts, not live economic data; the in-game guide discloses these are not forecasts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game UI, 20-space trade board, AI difficulty options, pass-and-play mode, market and policy actions, events, weather, investment, scoring, generated sound effects, and mobile action buttons.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Opened the trade desk in Playwright and confirmed the board, player ledger, market ticker, and dashboard render.

### Active
- Interactive verification remains incomplete: market/policy actions, dice roll, tile resolution, AI progression, and mobile layout have not been tested.
- Changes are uncommitted.

### Blocked
- Real online matchmaking/lobbies, live trade data, full music, and voice acting require backend/data/audio resources not present in the project.

## Next Move
1. Test the market and policy actions, dice roll, tile resolution, and AI turn progression in Playwright.
2. Check mobile layout and look for additional console errors; fix gameplay or UI issues found.
3. Optionally add a favicon or otherwise resolve the known `/favicon.ico` 404, then report assumptions and online-mode limitation.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game screens and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design and board/counter styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, AI, events, economy, sound, and interactions.

## Important Context
- Local testing URL: `http://localhost:3002`; server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Playwright successfully opened the site and trade desk; the only reported console error is `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico:0`.

## Objective
- Build a playable modern Australian trade strategy game inspired by Squatter, with trade, climate, policy, events, AI opponents, and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Original scope included live import/export data, solo AI difficulty levels, online modes and lobbies, animated dice, music/sound/voices/weather, and touchscreen controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone browser game with solo AI and local pass-and-play; online matchmaking is not implemented without a server.
- Use fictionalized market values and shifts, not live economic data; the in-game guide discloses these are not forecasts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created responsive game UI, 20-space trade board, AI difficulty options, pass-and-play mode, market and policy actions, events, weather, investment, scoring, generated sound effects, and mobile action buttons.
- `node --check game.js` passed; Playwright confirmed the trade desk renders.
- Playwright exercised a market purchase, local-first policy, dice roll, export tile resolution, and asset purchase; these interactions worked.

### Active
- Finish the current Playwright turn by continuing from the landing briefing, then verify AI progression and subsequent turn handling.
- Check mobile layout and re-test for console errors after addressing the known favicon 404.

### Blocked
- Real online matchmaking/lobbies, live trade data, full music, and voice acting require backend/data/audio resources not present in the project.

## Next Move
1. Click `CONTINUE` on the current “Market briefing” to check the AI turn and next quarter progression.
2. Test mobile layout and look for gameplay or UI issues; resolve `/favicon.ico` 404 if practical.
3. Report assumptions and the online-mode limitation.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, AI, events, economy, sound, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game screens and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and board styling.

## Important Context
- Local testing URL: `http://localhost:3002`; server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Playwright’s current game state is at the end of Quarter 01: You bought Tech, adopted Local First, rolled 5 + 4, landed on Beef & Grain, and invested A$24m; the landing briefing is open awaiting `CONTINUE`.
- Only observed console error is `Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (File not found) @ http://localhost:3002/favicon.ico:0`.
- Changes are uncommitted.

## Objective
- Build a playable modern Australian trade strategy game inspired by Squatter, featuring trade, climate, policy, events, AI opponents, and mobile controls.

## Requirements
- Original scope included live import/export data, solo AI difficulty levels, online modes and lobbies, animated dice, music/sound/voices/weather, and touchscreen controls.
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions and briefly note them at finish.

## Decisions
- Built a standalone browser game with solo AI and local pass-and-play; online matchmaking is not implemented without a server.
- Use fictionalized market values and shifts, not live economic data; the in-game guide discloses these are not forecasts.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created responsive game UI, 20-space trade board, AI difficulty options, pass-and-play mode, market and policy actions, events, weather, investment, scoring, generated sound effects, and mobile action buttons.
- `node --check game.js` passed; Playwright tested market purchase, local-first policy, dice roll, export tile resolution, asset purchase, AI turns, and progression to Quarter 02.
- Checked the mobile layout at 390×844; mobile action bar appeared, with no horizontal overflow reported. Mobile Market button opened the trade dialog.
- Added `favicon.svg` and linked it in `index.html` to address the observed `/favicon.ico` 404.

### Active
- Reload and recheck the browser console to confirm the favicon change removed the 404; the last console count predates the fix.
- Finish mobile interaction checks if needed.

### Blocked
- Real online matchmaking/lobbies, live trade data, full music, and voice acting require backend/data/audio resources not present in the project.

## Next Move
1. Reload `http://localhost:3002` and verify the favicon loads without console errors.
2. Optionally verify the mobile policy/roll buttons, then report assumptions and the online-mode limitation.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, AI, events, economy, sound, and interactions.
- `index.html`: Game screens and controls; favicon link.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and board styling.
- `favicon.svg`: Newly added game favicon.

## Important Context
- Local server is running at `http://localhost:3002` via `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Current Playwright state is Quarter 02, with the mobile Market dialog open; the latest AI progression completed and the next player turn is ready.
- Changes are uncommitted.

Identify exact DOM ids, rendering functions, setup controls, CSS patterns, and where market ticker, policy/modal, game end, sound toggle and turns can be extended for (1) online room create/join via REST polling, (2) external live quote ticker via backend API, (3) tax/accounting ledger, and (4) procedural music / spoken event commentary. content.text:
<subagent sessionID="ses_e565104b1ffeWWEhtNk1bH5lPf" state="completed">
## Implementation map

- **Setup / online-room controls:** [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html:31-40`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html) contains `.difficulty[data-level]`, `.mode-option[data-mode]`, and `#start-game`. The existing modes are solo and pass-and-play; their click handlers and `start()`/`makeGame()` are in [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js:39-41,71`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js). This is the natural UI extension point for a room option, room code, and join/create flow.
- **Game state and rendering:** `game.js` is one IIFE. `g` is initialized in `makeGame()`; `render()` updates the screen and calls `drawBoard()`, `drawPlayers()`, `drawMarket()`, and `drawResilience()` ([`game.js:39-46`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)). `#board`, `#players-list`, `#market-ticker`, and resilience elements are defined in [`index.html:51,56-57`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html).
- **Live quotes:** `drawMarket()` renders the four-item ticker in `#market-ticker` from `g.market` ([`game.js:45`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)). Prices currently start from local constants and are randomly shifted in `newQuarter()` ([`game.js:37,68`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)); there is no quote API or polling/WebSocket implementation.
- **Tax / accounting ledger:** `#players-list` sits under “NATIONAL LEDGER,” but `drawPlayers()` only shows player name, policy, asset count, cash, and an asset value ([`index.html:56`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html), [`game.js:44`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)). Transaction effects are spread across `trade()`, `setPolicy()`, `moveCurrent()`, `resolveTile()`, `newQuarter()`, event-card handlers, and AI logic ([`game.js:25-33,53-69`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)). There is no transaction-history or tax calculation layer; a ledger will need to record those distributed mutations or introduce a shared transaction mechanism.
- **Music / spoken commentary:** The existing `.sound-toggle` controls `audioOn`; `sfx()` produces short Web Audio oscillator effects ([`index.html:19`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html), [`game.js:50,71`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)). `addLog()` and `toast()` provide natural event hooks for commentary ([`game.js:48-49`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)). There is no procedural music system or speech synthesis.
- **Dialogs and visual patterns:** `modal()` injects dialog content into `#modal-root` ([`index.html:67`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/index.html), [`game.js:51`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)); `endGame()` renders the results modal ([`game.js:70`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)). CSS tokens are at the start of [`/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css:2`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/style.css); the stylesheet is densely compressed, with responsive breakpoints at 1050px, 760px, and 390px (lines 8–10).

## Risks to account for

- **Online state:** The browser currently owns all game state and turn logic. A server-backed room needs authoritative state and safeguards against stale updates, duplicate actions, and turn-order races.
- **Dynamic content:** Several render paths use interpolated `innerHTML`, including player rows, logs, ticker items, and modals. Escape or safely insert server-supplied names, prices, and commentary.
- **Accounting correctness:** Cash and inventory changes occur in multiple paths, including event effects and AI turns. A ledger or tax calculation can miss transactions unless those paths are consistently captured.
- **Live-data behavior:** Define the source, units, refresh cadence, and fallback for quotes, and distinguish real market data from the game’s current fictional values.
- **Audio and speech:** Web Audio already resumes a suspended context; music and speech also need user-consent and browser-autoplay handling.
- **Existing documentation:** The in-game help text says online matchmaking requires a server and that this build only includes solo AI and local pass-and-play ([`game.js:71`](/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/game.js)).
</subagent>

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the Australian trade strategy game beyond its existing browser-only version, including real-time market quotes, a tax system, music, sound, voice commentary, and online multiplayer/lobbies.

## Requirements
- User explicitly requested the remaining features “no matter what”; proceed with reasonable assumptions without asking clarifying questions.
- Preserve the existing game and extend it rather than replacing it.

## Decisions
- Yahoo Finance search results identify `TIO=F` as an iron ore benchmark, but Yahoo has no official public API; quotes need a robust source/fallback and clear source, units, and freshness labels.
- ATO search results identify Australian company tax rates of 25% for eligible base-rate entities and 30% otherwise for 2025–26; game tax rules should be disclosed as a simplified simulation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Existing game includes solo AI, pass-and-play, trade/policy actions, events, weather, investment, scoring, generated sound effects, animated dice, mobile controls, and responsive layout.
- Prior browser checks covered core game progression and mobile layout; favicon `favicon.svg` was confirmed loaded.
- Explored integration points in `game.js` and `index.html`; no changes have yet been made for the newly requested features.

### Active
- Add a backend/API layer for live market quotes and online rooms, then integrate them into the frontend.
- Add a tax/accounting ledger, richer music and sound, and opt-in spoken commentary.
- Update setup, gameplay UI, help, and documentation to explain sources, data freshness, and simplified mechanics.

### Blocked
- Real quotes depend on an external provider’s availability and terms; Yahoo’s endpoint is unofficial and may fail or be delayed. Provide clear stale/demo fallback instead of presenting fictional prices as live.
- Online rooms require a running server; no server or networking dependencies exist yet.

## Next Move
1. Implement a minimal Node HTTP server with quote-provider proxy/cache and multiplayer room endpoints.
2. Extend setup and game state/UI for online play, live quote source/freshness, and tax ledger/accounting.
3. Add opt-in procedural music and synthesized sounds plus browser speech-synthesis commentary.
4. Test the game, server endpoints, fallback behavior, multiplayer synchronization, and mobile interactions; update help and README.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing game state, turn flow, trade, policy, AI, events, ticker, sounds, and help.
- `index.html`: Setup controls, game dashboard, ticker, mobile actions, and dialog root.
- `style.css`: Existing visual system and responsive layout.
- `README.md`: Project overview and documentation.

## Important Context
- Current app is a vanilla HTML/CSS/JavaScript game with no installed `ws`, `express`, or `socket.io` package; Node.js is available.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Complete the existing Australian trade strategy game with market benchmarks, a tax ledger, richer sound/music and optional voice, and online two-player rooms.

## Requirements
- Preserve and extend the existing game; proceed with reasonable assumptions.
- Do not present simulated prices as real market data; disclose quote source and freshness.
- Explain that game tax rules are a simplified simulation.

## Decisions
- Keep the game’s A$m prices simulated and separate from an external iron ore benchmark; Yahoo Finance’s `TIO=F` chart endpoint is unofficial and may be delayed or unavailable.
- Use a lightweight Node HTTP server for static files, quote proxying, and in-memory online rooms.
- Model game tax as a simplified 25% rate on positive quarterly cashflow, with capital investment added back.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `server.js` with static hosting, `/api/health`, a cached Yahoo iron ore quote endpoint with unavailable/stale responses, and in-memory two-player room create/join/state endpoints.
- Added setup UI for online rooms, audio/music/voice toggles, connection status, a tax-ledger button, and quote source/status display.
- Added styling for the new controls, quote display, and ledger.
- Began frontend support for room creation/joining, state polling/sync, quote fetching, audio/music/speech, and online-aware player state.

### Active
- Finish frontend integration: bind online controls, complete turn-based synchronization, implement quarterly tax settlement and ledger modal, and connect music/voice toggles and commentary.
- Update help and `README.md` for live quote caveats, simplified taxes, online server setup, and audio features.
- Test game progression, server endpoints, quote fallbacks, online synchronization, and mobile interactions.

### Blocked
- Live quotes depend on Yahoo’s unofficial endpoint and may be delayed or unavailable; the server provides an explicit fallback rather than simulated live values.
- Online rooms require `node server.js` and are in-memory, so they do not persist across server restarts.

## Next Move
1. Complete `game.js` integration, especially missing `openLedger`, online event bindings, tax settlement, and syncing in `advance()`.
2. Run syntax checks and smoke-test the server and room/quote endpoints.
3. Exercise solo, pass-and-play, online, and mobile flows; document setup and limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Existing game plus partial online, quote, sound, and voice integration.
- `server.js`: New static/API server, quote proxy, and room endpoints.
- `index.html`: Setup controls and game dashboard additions.
- `style.css`: Styles for new controls and quote/ledger displays.
- `README.md`: Needs feature and run instructions.

## Important Context
- The repository’s game files were uncommitted/untracked before these edits; the new work remains uncommitted.
- `game.js` currently references `openLedger` before it is implemented, and the new UI controls are not yet fully wired.
- Room state is synchronized through REST polling; server rooms support two players and exist only in memory.

## Objective
- Complete the Australian trade strategy game with a market benchmark, simplified tax ledger, richer audio and optional voice, and online two-player rooms.

## Requirements
- Keep simulated A$m game prices distinct from external market data; disclose quote source and freshness.
- Explain that the game’s tax rules are a simplified simulation.
- Preserve and extend the existing game using reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use Yahoo Finance’s unofficial `TIO=F` chart endpoint for the iron ore benchmark; it may be delayed or unavailable, with explicit fallback messaging.
- Use a lightweight Node server for static hosting, quote proxying, and in-memory online rooms.
- Simulate tax as 25% of positive quarterly cashflow, adding capital investment back before calculating taxable flow.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `server.js` static hosting, health and quote endpoints, and in-memory two-player room APIs.
- Added setup and dashboard UI for online play, audio/voice toggles, quote status, and a tax ledger.
- Implemented core quote display, online room create/join and polling/sync logic, tax settlement and ledger modal in `game.js`.
- Added styling for the new controls and displays.

### Active
- Finish wiring online controls, music and voice toggles/commentary, and update stale help text.
- Test solo, pass-and-play, online turns, quarterly taxes, quote fallbacks, and mobile interactions.
- Document startup, audio, quote limitations, and simplified tax rules in `README.md`.

### Blocked
- Live benchmark availability depends on Yahoo’s unofficial endpoint; fallback messaging is implemented.
- Online rooms require `node server.js` and are in-memory, so they do not persist across server restarts.

## Next Move
1. Wire remaining controls and commentary in `game.js`; revise help text and `README.md`.
2. Run syntax checks and smoke-test server, quote fallback, and room endpoints.
3. Exercise game modes, quarter-end tax settlement, online turn handoffs, and mobile UI.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, online synchronization, quote display, tax settlement and ledger; remaining event wiring and testing.
- `server.js`: Static server, quote proxy, and room APIs.
- `index.html`: Setup controls and game dashboard additions.
- `style.css`: Styles for new controls and displays.
- `README.md`: Needs feature and run instructions.

## Important Context
- Project files are uncommitted and were untracked in the latest `git status`.
- `node --check game.js` and `node --check server.js` passed before the latest edits; rerun after changes.
- Recent edits added tax settlement and `stateUpdatedAt` handling for room synchronization; these have not yet been verified.

## Run locally

Requires Node.js 18 or newer (the server uses the built-in `fetch` API). From the project directory:

```sh
node server.js
```

Then open [http://localhost:3002](http://localhost:3002). Set `PORT` to use another port, for example `PORT=8080 node server.js`. The server hosts the game, proxies the optional benchmark quote and keeps online rooms in memory.

## Game modes and audio

- **Solo vs AI** offers three AI difficulty levels.
- **Pass & play** lets two people take turns on one device.
- **Online room** lets a host create a room and share its six-character code with one opponent. Both players need to reach the same server. Rooms are in-memory and are lost when the Node process restarts; this is a lightweight demo, not durable matchmaking.
- The header controls independently toggle sound effects, a generated background tone sequence, and optional browser speech commentary. Browser support and available voices vary; speech requires a browser with the Web Speech API.

## Market benchmark and game prices

In-game commodity prices are fictional, simulated A$ millions and are never derived from the external quote. The optional iron-ore benchmark uses Yahoo Finance's unofficial `TIO=F` chart endpoint. Yahoo may delay, change, or block the endpoint; the interface identifies the source and quote time and labels stale data, or reports the benchmark unavailable rather than presenting it as live. The benchmark is informational only and does not change gameplay prices.

## Simplified tax ledger

At each quarter settlement, the game charges 25% of positive quarterly cashflow. It adds capital investment back when calculating that flow; negative or zero quarterly flows incur no tax. This is a deliberately simplified game mechanic, not Australian tax law, tax advice, or a representation of actual business tax treatment.

## Objective
- Complete the Australian trade strategy game with an external market benchmark, simplified tax ledger, richer audio and optional voice, and online two-player rooms.

## Requirements
- Keep simulated A$m game prices distinct from external market data; disclose quote source and freshness.
- Explain that game tax rules are a simplified simulation.
- Preserve and extend the existing game using reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use Yahoo Finance’s unofficial `TIO=F` chart endpoint for the iron ore benchmark; clearly message delays, stale quotes, or unavailability.
- Use a lightweight Node server for static hosting, quote proxying, and in-memory online rooms.
- Simulate tax as 25% of positive quarterly cashflow, adding capital investment back before calculating taxable flow.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added `server.js` static hosting, health and quote endpoints, and in-memory two-player room APIs.
- Added online setup, sound/music/voice toggles, quote status, and a tax ledger to the UI.
- Wired mode-dependent setup, room creation/joining, online turn ownership and polling, audio toggles, and spoken turn/landing/event commentary in `game.js`.
- Added README instructions for startup, game modes, audio, quote limitations, room behavior, and simplified tax rules.
- Updated help text; preserved escaped player names, room update timestamps, `musicStop()`, and speech API guards.
- `node --check game.js && node --check server.js` passed.

### Active
- Smoke-test server health, quote fallback, room endpoints, gameplay/online turn flows, and mobile interactions.
- Review final changes and verify the UI behavior in a browser if available.

### Blocked
- Live benchmark availability depends on Yahoo’s unofficial endpoint; fallback messaging is implemented.
- Online rooms require `node server.js` and are in-memory, so they do not persist across server restarts.

## Next Move
1. Run server and smoke-test health, quote fallback, and create/join/state room APIs.
2. Test solo, pass-and-play, and both online player turns, including audio toggles and mobile controls.
3. Review the final diff and report any remaining limitations.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, online synchronization, quote display, tax ledger, event wiring, audio and voice.
- `server.js`: Static server, quote proxy, and room APIs.
- `index.html`: Setup controls and game dashboard.
- `style.css`: UI styling.
- `README.md`: Startup and feature documentation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed `README.md` modified and project files including `game.js`, `server.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css` untracked.
- Online clients now treat both players as human and enable controls only for the local player’s turn; remote room state is polled and applied when that client’s turn arrives.

29:

31: 
32: - **Solo vs AI** offers three AI difficulty levels.
33: - **Pass & play** lets two people take turns on one device.
34: - **Online room** lets a host create a room and share its six-character code with one opponent. Both players need to reach the same server. Rooms are in-memory and are lost when the Node process restarts; this is a lightweight demo, not durable matchmaking.

38:

The optional iron-ore benchmark uses Yahoo Finance's unofficial `TIO=F` chart endpoint. 42:

def js(sid,script): return call(sid,'POST','/execute/sync',{'script':script,'args':[]})

20: ## Run locally
21: 
22: Requires Node.js 18 or newer (the server uses the built-in `fetch` API). From the project directory:
23: 
24: ```sh
25: node server.js
26: ```
27: 
28: Then open [http://localhost:3002](http://localhost:3002). Set `PORT` to use another port, for example `PORT=8080 node server.js`. The server hosts the game, proxies the optional benchmark quote and keeps online rooms in memory.
29: 
30: ## Game modes and audio
31: 
32: - **Solo vs AI** offers three AI difficulty levels.
33: - **Pass & play** lets two people take turns on one device.
34: - **Online room** lets a host create a room and share its six-character code with one opponent. Both players need to reach the same server. Rooms are in-memory and are lost when the Node process restarts; this is a lightweight demo, not durable matchmaking.
35: - The header controls independently toggle sound effects, a generated background tone sequence, and optional browser speech commentary. Browser support and available voices vary; speech requires a browser with the Web Speech API.
36: 
37: ## Market benchmark and game prices
38: 
39: In-game commodity prices are fictional, simulated A$ millions and are never derived from the external quote. The optional iron-ore benchmark uses Yahoo Finance's unofficial `TIO=F` chart endpoint. Yahoo may delay, change, or block the endpoint; the interface identifies the source and quote time and labels stale data, or reports the benchmark unavailable rather than presenting it as live. The benchmark is informational only and does not change gameplay prices.
40: 
41: ## Simplified tax ledger
42: 
43: At each quarter settlement, the game charges 25% of positive quarterly cashflow. It adds capital investment back when calculating that flow; negative or zero quarterly flows incur no tax. This is a deliberately simplified game mechanic, not Australian tax law, tax advice, or a representation of actual business tax treatment.

## Objective
- Complete the Australian trade strategy game with an external market benchmark, simplified tax ledger, richer audio, and online two-player rooms.

## Requirements
- Keep simulated A$m game prices distinct from external market data; disclose quote source and freshness.
- Explain that game tax rules are a simplified simulation.
- Preserve and extend the existing game using reasonable assumptions.

## Decisions
- Use Yahoo Finance’s unofficial `TIO=F` chart endpoint for the iron ore benchmark; clearly label delayed, stale, or unavailable quotes.
- Use a lightweight Node server for static hosting, quote proxying, and in-memory online rooms.
- Simulate tax as 25% of positive quarterly cashflow, adding capital investment back before calculating taxable flow.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added server, game modes, online room APIs, quote display, tax ledger, audio controls, voice commentary, responsive UI, and README documentation.
- Fixed unescaped player names in end-game ranking and winner text in `game.js` using `esc()`.
- Browser-tested solo play, pass-and-play, online room creation/joining and synchronized turns, audio controls, and mobile interactions; all passed.
- `node --check game.js`, `node --check server.js`, and `git diff --check` passed.

### Active
- Finish reviewing the final changes and summarize remaining limitations.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Review the final diff and remaining limitations.
2. Report completion and note that changes remain uncommitted.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Game logic, online synchronization, quote display, tax ledger, audio, and escaped end-game ranking.
- `server.js`: Static server, quote proxy, freshness handling, and room APIs.
- `index.html`: Setup controls and game dashboard.
- `style.css`: UI styling and responsive layouts.
- `README.md`: Startup and feature documentation.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted: `README.md` is modified; `.gitignore`, `Agents.md`, `capture.sh`, `favicon.svg`, `game.js`, `index.html`, `server.js`, `start.sh`, `startup.sh`, and `style.css` are untracked.
- The initial browser wait failure was caused by the test harness not returning JavaScript results; the corrected tests passed.
- Port 3004 was already occupied; browser tests used the existing service serving this project.
- Yahoo’s quote endpoint is unofficial and may delay, change, or block data; online rooms are in-memory and do not persist across server restarts.
